permission.description: Reports the engine's base URL and boot token to the main window. With the token, every engine route is reachable (docs/00 §6.3), so this permission is the reason the local-origin bypass below had to be closed.
Reports whether the engine process is up, without starting it.
Lists the eight role slots and their per-role configuration, with API keys redacted (docs/00 §6.4).
Writes one role's configuration. Read-modify-write over the same key, so a lost race is a lost update rather than a credential leak.
Restores missing or malformed role slots to their defaults. Destructive to local state by design, so it is granted explicitly rather than swept in by a wildcard.
Probes a provider connection and reports the failure, without persisting anything.
Starts a PTY the user asked for. A terminal is arbitrary code execution by another name, so the grant names it rather than inheriting it.
Writes keystrokes to an existing PTY.
Resizes an existing PTY so the shell redraws to fit.
Opens a browser webview. The webview itself holds no permission (capabilities/browser.json is empty), so this grants the *main window* the ability to open one — it does not grant that page anything.
Navigates an existing browser webview, through the same loopback guard as `open`.
Closes a browser webview by tab id.

set.description: Every command this app defines, as thirteen named permissions and no wildcard. The point of listing them one by one is that a command added to `invoke_handler!` without a line here does not become reachable — it is stripped from the handler at compile time, and src-tauri/src/browser.rs fails the build's test leg if the two lists ever differ. Permissions are not where a window/webview is decided: this set is referenced only by capabilities/default.json, whose `windows` is `["main"]`, and capabilities/browser.json keeps an empty list for `browser-*`.
